title: Epicentre vs Hypocentre Quiz
description: Watched the episode on epicentres? See if you can tell the epicentre from the hypocentre.

questions.question: What does the "epicentre" in the news actually mean?
options: The point underground where the fault starts to break
The point on the surface directly above the hypocentre
The place where the shaking is strongest
questions.explanation: The point underground where the rupture begins is the hypocentre. The epicentre is the spot on the surface right above it.

questions.question: Three seismic stations each draw a circle. Where is the epicentre?
options: Wherever is closest to the nearest station
At the centres of the circles
questions.explanation: Each circle shows how far the earthquake is from that station, so the one point all three pass through is the epicentre.

questions.question: What do we call an earthquake 0–70 km deep?
questions.explanation: 0–70 km is shallow, 70–300 km is intermediate and 300–700 km is deep.

questions.question: Lots of earthquakes are listed at exactly 10 km deep. Why, usually?
options: The crust breaks most easily at 10 km
When the depth can't be worked out, a fixed depth is filled in
Seismic stations are buried 10 km underground
questions.explanation: Without enough stations close by, the depth of a shallow earthquake is hard to pin down, so agencies put in 10 km as a stand-in.

questions.question: Why isn't the epicentre enough to describe the 2004 Sumatra–Andaman earthquake?
options: The rupture ran along the fault for more than 1,000 km
questions.explanation: The hypocentre was only the starting line. A whole stretch of fault slipped, so the worst shaking wasn't necessarily near the epicentre.
